escena.titulo: Carrying capacity: J and S curves

turnos.t: With no limiting factors, growth is exponential: a J-curve, like yeast with plenty of food. It can't last; the population crashes. With limiting factors, you get an S-curve: fast growth, then it slows as density-dependent factors like competition increase near K, and it levels off. Real populations often overshoot K and oscillate around it, because of time lags.
And what keeps it near K?

Negative feedback. Above K, competition increases, the death rate rises and the birth rate falls, so the population returns towards K. And r-strategists, like dandelions, have many small offspring and fluctuate; K-strategists, like elephants, have few offspring with more care and stay near K. Most species sit on a continuum.
